children.translated_text: [That mind] by which this past, present, and future universe is all encompassed by the immortal, by which the sacrifice is spread with seven priests — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

By which the wise, the industrious, perform deeds in the sacrifice, [by which] the wise [act] in the assemblies, that wondrous being [dwelling] within creatures — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

That which is wisdom, and consciousness, and firmness, that which is the immortal light within creatures, without which no deed whatsoever is performed — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
That divine [mind] which travels far when one is awake, and goes just as far when one is asleep — that far-ranging one, the one light of lights — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

In which the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> [verses] are established like spokes in the nave of a chariot, in which is woven the entire consciousness of creatures — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
That which guides men like a good charioteer [guides] horses with the reins, like a steed — that which is seated in the heart, swift and swiftest — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

That sixth of the three-hundred [days], the body of the sacrifice, the secret, the primordial [altar] with nine navels, that which is beyond ten and thirty-five — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
Those fives, fifteens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, and hundred-millions — they are the bricks building the body of the sacrifice — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), sun-colored, beyond darkness; the wise perceive His source — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
By which the wise, the learned, act through speech, mind, and deed, by which living beings come together in mutual understanding — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

Those [powers] which are the mind, the heart, and those deities who move about diversely in the atmosphere, those which move through the ear and the eyes — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

By which the mighty heaven and earth and the atmosphere, by which the mountains and the quarters and directions [are upheld], by which this world is pervaded [in the knowledge] of creatures — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

By which all these [beings] of the world have come into existence, by which even the gods [arose from] the great <s>Jātavedas</s> (all-knowing fire), that very single light of fire and austerity — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: tyaṃ cāprameyaṃ ca vyaktāvyaktaparaṃ ca yat

children.translated_text: That which is inconceivable and immeasurable, beyond the manifest and the unmanifest, that knowledge subtler than the subtle — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: asti vināśayitvā sarvam idaṃ nāsti punas tathaivā dṛṣṭaṃ dhruvaṃ
asti nāsti hitaṃ madhyamaṃ padaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: Having destroyed all this 'it exists,' [there remains] 'it does not exist,' and again just so the permanent is seen; 'exists' and 'does not exist' — the beneficent middle state — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: sti nāsti sarvaṃ vā idaṃ guhyam
asti nāsti parāt paro yat paraṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: 'Exists' and 'does not exist' — the reversed stream; 'exists' and 'does not exist' — all this is indeed secret; 'exists' and 'does not exist' — that which is beyond the beyond, the supreme — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: parāt parataraṃ yasya tatparāc caiva tat paraṃ
tatparāt paratojñeyaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: That which is higher than the highest, beyond which is indeed that supreme, that which is to be known beyond that beyond — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: parāt parataro brahma tatparāt parato hariḥ
tatparāt parato hy eṣa tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is higher than the highest; <s>Hari</s> is beyond that beyond; and beyond that beyond indeed is He [<s>Śiva</s>] — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: gobhir juṣṭo dhanena hy āyuṣā ca balena ca
prajayā paśubhiḥ puṣkalādyaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: Blessed with cattle, wealth, long life, and strength, with progeny, with livestock — [may there be] abundance and foremost [fortune] — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: oṃkāraṃ param ātmānaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: The purified <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) is eternally the supreme, the highest <s>Puruṣa</s>; <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the supreme Self — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: yo vai vedādiṣu gāyatrī sarvavyāpī maheśvaraḥ
yad dviruktaṃ tathādvyaiśyaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: He who in the <s>Vedas</s> and the like is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the all-pervading <s>Maheśvara</s>; that which is uttered twice, and likewise the double-glory — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: yo vai veda mahādevam paramaṃ puruṣottamaṃ
yaḥ sarvaṃ yasya cit sarvaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: He who truly knows <s>Mahādeva</s>, the supreme, the highest <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is everything and whose consciousness is everything — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: sau sarveṣu vedeṣu pathate hy aja īśvaraḥ
akāyo nirguṇo dhyātvā tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: He who is recited in all the <s>Vedas</s>, the unborn Lord; having meditated on [Him who is] bodiless and beyond qualities — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: ti tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: On the delightful peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, in the auspicious abode of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the deities there rejoice — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: ṭhaṃ trinetraṃ ca tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: Those who are radiant like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, indeed, abiding on the mountain — [may we behold] the blue-throated, three-eyed [<s>Śiva</s>] — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: utpātitaṃ jagad vyāptaṃ tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: From <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, the three worlds, moving and unmoving — the entire world pervaded — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: ti tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who always meditate on this <s>Śivasaṃkalpa</s> (auspicious resolve) — they will attain supreme liberation — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

children.text: dhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt tan me manaḥ śivasaṃkalpam astu
children.translated_text: We worship the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>), the fragrant, the nourisher of prosperity. Like a cucumber from its stem, may I be liberated from death, not from immortality — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
